title: Trauma Research
originAuthor: Bessel van der Kolk, Peter Levine, Pat Ogden, Judith Herman
summary: Trauma is stored in the body, not just the mind. Defensive responses that were interrupted or overwhelmed during threat continue to seek completion, shaping physiology, perception, and behavior long after danger has passed.

content.title: Core Concept
content.content: Trauma research, pioneered by van der Kolk, Levine, Ogden, and Herman, established that traumatic experiences are encoded in the body's implicit memory systems. When threat overwhelms the nervous system's capacity to respond, defensive actions (fight, flight, freeze, fawn) remain incomplete. These unfinished responses continue to organize physiology and behavior, creating patterns that persist until the body can complete what it started.

content.title: How TEG-Blue Integrates This
content.content: TEG-Blue maps trauma responses onto the Four-Mode Gradient: fight and flight as active Protection, freeze and fawn as collapsed Protection or early Control patterns. Chronic trauma calibrates the system toward Control or Domination — strategies that manage threat through power rather than returning to Connection. The framework explains why cognitive insight alone rarely resolves trauma: the body must complete its defensive response and experience safety before the system can update.
